commit.subject: LU-15864 ofd: recreate lost objects for all requests
commit.message:
LU-15864 ofd: recreate lost objects for all requests

An OST restart loses the objects it had precreated but not
committed. Precreate and write replay recreate them during OST
recovery, and the MDT's orphan cleanup does so once the MDT is
out of its own recovery. When the MDT restarts too, as when MDTs and
OSTs share a server, that can be well after the OST has
finished recovery. A request reaching the OST in between finds
its object missing and fails with -ENOENT. A write with a
cached lock fails this way and the application gets -EIO; a
setattr from the MDT is dropped as if the object were gone.
Only lock enqueue handled the window, by returning -EINPROGRESS
since LU-15195.

Recreate a missing object, and those below it in its sequence,
if its ID is above the OST's LAST_ID and the MDT has sent no
create for the sequence since the OST restarted, within the hard
recovery timeout. An MDT that takes part in the OST's recovery
replays its precreates first, so this recreates objects only for
an MDT that is absent or restarted, limiting the orphans that a
client evicted by the MDT can leave. Do this for read,
write, getattr, setattr, punch, fallocate, sync, seek, fiemap
and ladvise, using a local transaction so that a request is not
given a transno for it. Do not recreate while LFSCK rebuilds
LAST_ID, nor more than OST_MAX_PRECREATE objects, the most that
orphan cleanup destroys if the MDT never used them: write replay
used to recreate any gap. Outside recovery, stop after
DISK_TIMEOUT and return -EINPROGRESS so that the client resends.
ofd_object_recreate() and ofd_object_find_recreate() do this,
with ofd_lseek_hdl() wrapping tgt_lseek().

Lock enqueue cannot create the object, as orphan cleanup inits
LVBs while holding the sequence's create lock. Its -EINPROGRESS
kept stat and chown of a lost object waiting for orphan cleanup,
however long the MDT took to recover. Give a lost object the
empty LVB of the object it will be recreated as instead, using
ofd_object_lost(). A missing object at or below LAST_ID was
destroyed, and still gets -ENOENT. A destroy of a lost object
still makes clients discard their cached data, which a later write
would otherwise recreate the object with.

Add replay-ost-single tests 12c to 12m, which fail over the
MDT and the OST together with orphan cleanup delayed and check
that each kind of request succeeds, and that an unlink discards
cached data. Pin their directory to MDT0000
and require OST0000 so that allocation cannot use other targets.
Keep statfs behind the replay barrier from reporting read-only
space, which otherwise redirects ZFS allocations to another OST.
Wait for cached read-only state from preceding replay tests before
the initial write. Limit OST debug logging during recovery so the
recreation messages are not overwritten before they are checked,
and read them also from the log a long recovery dumps.
